research.abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent, and undernutrition is a major modifiable risk factor. Serum proteomics can capture systemic host recovery during therapy, but whether baseline BMI-defined undernutrition alters this trajectory is unclear. Methods We reanalysed processed longitudinal tandem-mass-tag serum proteomics from 30 adults with pulmonary tuberculosis and durable cure sampled at baseline and weeks 8, 17, 26 and 52. Thirteen participants had baseline BMI <18.5 kg/m² and 17 had BMI ≥18.5 kg/m². Protein-level analyses evaluated baseline differences and week-specific within-participant change; module and recovery-axis models evaluated BMI-by-time interactions, with random-intercept mixed models added as a repeated-measures sensitivity analysis. Three complementary treatment-responsive modules were integrated into an exploratory, nonredundant 36-protein nutritional-metabolic summary axis. Results The reconstructed dataset contained 1,923 quantified features across 150 participant-visits. Inflammatory/acute-phase and metal-handling/nutritional-immunity module scores declined during follow-up, whereas lipid/apolipoprotein-transport, nutritional-carrier and endocrine-immunometabolic scores increased. In the primary week-specific paired-change analyses, no protein-level between-BMI difference in longitudinal change survived false-discovery-rate correction; no curated-module BMI-by-time interaction survived correction. The 36-protein summary axis increased in both BMI strata from week 17 onward. In a random-intercept model without interaction, the BMI <18.5 kg/m² stratum had a lower average axis score across visits than the BMI ≥18.5 kg/m² comparison stratum, although the confidence interval included zero (difference −1.34, 95% CI −2.76 to 0.08; p = .064). Categorical and continuous BMI-by-time interaction tests did not detect differential axis trajectories. Conclusions Tuberculosis treatment was accompanied by broad longitudinal remodelling of circulating inflammatory and nutritional-metabolic protein systems. An exploratory 36-protein summary axis increased in both baseline BMI strata, while formal interaction tests did not detect BMI-dependent trajectories and remained too imprecise to establish equivalence. BMI should be regarded as an anthropometric proxy rather than a comprehensive measure of nutritional state. The defined axis provides a framework for prospective validation alongside direct measures of body composition, micronutrients, treatment exposure and clinical outcomes. Clinical relevance Microbiological cure does not necessarily describe the pace or completeness of host recovery from tuberculosis disease. This study summarizes longitudinal lipid-transport, nutritional-carrier and endocrine-immunometabolic changes in a serum recovery axis that can be carried forward for testing in independent cohorts. Baseline BMI was not detectably associated with the axis at baseline in this small cohort and should be regarded as an available anthropometric proxy rather than a comprehensive measure of nutritional state. Future studies should evaluate the axis alongside detailed nutritional phenotyping, pharmacology, post-tuberculosis morbidity and relapse risk.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) imposes a substantial burden on health systems and society. Although early detection and guideline-recommended management can improve outcomes, opportunities remain to enhance management in primary care. Aim To evaluate CKD prevalence, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), and monitoring in Irish primary care. Design and Setting Retrospective cohort study using community-based electronic health records (EHR) from the CRADLE database, across 66 Irish practices. Methods Active adults aged ≥20 years on 30 July 2025 were included. CKD prevalence was determined using estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and/or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR). Descriptive analyses of epidemiology, prescribing, and monitoring were conducted. Results Of 468,534 adults, 19,382 met the criteria of laboratory-confirmed CKD: age- and sex-standardised prevalence was 5.36%. 74.0% of laboratory-confirmed CKD patients have ≥1 cardiometabolic comorbidities. Within 12 months of laboratory-confirmed CKD, monitoring increased over time, with 66.0% of patients receiving follow-up eGFR test and 15.1% receiving uACR test, falling to 6.6% among patients without type 2 diabetes (T2DM). Among GDMT-eligible CKD patients, 64.0% received any renin-angiotensin-aldosterone inhibitors (RAASi) and 30.9% received any sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) after they met their prescription eligibility for CKD, but SGLT2i use dropped to 9.4% among those without T2DM or heart failure. Conclusion CKD and cardiometabolic comorbidities impose a substantial burden in Irish primary care. Despite improved kidney function testing, albuminuria testing remained low, particularly in non-diabetic patients, and GDMT use was suboptimal. Improving albuminuria testing and timely GDMT offers important opportunities to improve CKD outcomes in Irish primary care.

research.abstract: Purpose Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) covers multiple drug resistance-associated regions, but drug-organized reports can duplicate variants across drugs and disperse a patient's variants. Through nomenclature standardization and cross-drug deduplication, we reconstructed nonredundant patient-level variant profiles and characterized multigene co-occurrence, molecular variant complexity, and reported frequency patterns. Patients and methods This single-center retrospective descriptive study included each patient's earliest eligible mutation-positive tuberculosis tNGS report from 2024-2025. The analysis dataset comprised report-derived information and did not include raw sequencing data or systematically paired phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST) results. Variants were standardized using the 2023 World Health Organization catalogue, H37Rv coordinates, and Human Genome Variation Society recommendations. Duplicate patient-gene-variant records were collapsed into unique patient-variant events while retaining drug annotations. Eight mutually exclusive, exhaustive combinations were defined from RIF (rpoB), INH (katG and/or inhA), and FQ (gyrA and/or gyrB) axes. Results Fifty-seven patients contributed 180 unique patient-variant events involving nine genes and 56 standardized variants. rpoB (84.2%) and katG (64.9%) were the leading genes. The leading variants were katG p.Ser315Thr (63.2%), rpsL p.Lys43Arg (29.8%), and rpoB p.Ser450Leu (26.3%), which together accounted for 37.8% of all events; 33 of 56 variants occurred in only one patient. Seven of the eight RIF/INH/FQ combinations were observed. RIF+/INH+/FQ- was most common (31/57, 54.4%), whereas RIF+/INH+/FQ+ had the highest median numbers of genes and variants (both 5.0). Twenty-three events in 16 patients had reported frequencies below 100%, and pncA- and gyrA-associated events accounted for 60.9%. Conclusion In this mutation-positive cohort, patient-level reconstruction integrated annotations of the same variant across drugs and characterized hotspots and a long tail of variants, multigene co-occurrence within RIF/INH/FQ combinations, and report-derived frequency patterns. This traceable data structure may support laboratory report review and future genotype-phenotype studies.

research.abstract: Microsporidia are single-celled, obligately intracellular eukaryotic parasites of growing importance. Many aspects of their biology remain enigmatic, partly because of difficulties in sampling, culturing, and experimentally manipulating them. Here, we continue efforts to generate microsporidian genomes from serendipitously infected organisms sequenced for biodiversity genomics initiatives, such as the Darwin Tree of Life Project. We present 25 new microsporidian genomes: 14 biologically complete, including several at (near-)chromosome level, and 11 partial. Using RNA-seq data for three published genomes we identify Prokka as a suitable ab initio annotation approach for Microsporidia. Consistently annotating all available genomes, we investigate gene-content diversity across microsporidian clades. We find that the microsporidian pangenome exhibits extreme diversity, and that current genomic data substantially undersample the group's proteome space. Neither GC content nor genome span consistently explains orthogroup number across lineages, suggesting different evolutionary pressures. We find few one-to-one orthogroups in Microsporidia, as well as few orthogroups that are both lineage-specific and conserved across most species within a given lineage. Finally, Hi-C data confirm that tetraploid Amblyosporida microsporidia occur as two equivalent diploid units. In contrast, one Enterocytozoonida tetraploid genome suggests that all four genome copies occur within a single nucleus (a 'monokaryon'), confirming a previous proposal.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conduct multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analyses of 63,415 cases of Europeans and East Asians, and identified 60 previously unreported susceptibility loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing, and alternative polyadenylation analyses using RNA-sequencing data from normal colon tissues of 707 Europeans and 364 East Asians, we identify 441 candidate risk genes, including 324 not previously implicated by GWAS or TWAS, of which 291 were further supported by colocalization or summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analyses. These genes converge on pathways central to IBD pathogenesis (e.g., immune regulation), with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. We further identify 44 druggable genes linked to 221 approved drugs or Phase II/III clinical-stage compounds. Our findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and provide insights for future research relevant to precision medicine for IBD.

research.abstract: Background. Spray-induced gene silencing (SIGS), in which double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) sprayed onto a crop is taken up by a fungal pathogen and silences an essential gene, is advancing as a biopesticide strategy. A recurring ambition is a broad-spectrum dsRNA: a single construct, directed at a conserved housekeeping gene, that controls several pathogens at once. Because silencing is driven by Dicer-processed small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) of roughly 21 nucleotides, the feasibility of this ambition depends on whether the target gene is conserved between pathogens at siRNA-length resolution, not merely at the level of overall gene identity. That resolution has not been mapped across the fungal plant-pathogen tree. Results. We screened eleven canonical antifungal dsRNA target genes of Fusarium graminearum (three CYP51 sterol 14-alpha-demethylases, six chitin synthases and two beta-tubulins) for perfect 21-nucleotide identity against the transcriptomes of twelve fungal plant pathogens spanning four taxonomic classes (Sordariomycetes, Leotiomycetes, Dothideomycetes and Basidiomycota). Of 27,116 candidate siRNA start positions across the eleven genes, only 2,108 (7.8%) were conserved as a perfect 21-mer in even one other pathogen, 148 in at least three, twelve in at least seven, and none in eight or more. Conservation decayed steeply with phylogenetic distance: the congeneric F. oxysporum shared 1,209 sites, other Sordariomycetes 262-313, Leotiomycetes and Dothideomycetes 62-204, Basidiomycota 41-48, and the reduced-genome obligate biotroph Blumeria graminis just one. The beta-tubulins carried the most broadly conserved individual sites (shared by up to seven pathogens), whereas CYP51C was the least conserved (shared by at most one). Even for the congener, perfect-match conservation covered only 4.5% of target positions and was concentrated in discrete windows rather than spread along the gene. Conclusions. At the siRNA-length resolution that governs silencing, perfect-match conservation of canonical antifungal targets is scarce and strongly clade-limited. A perfect-match broad-spectrum dsRNA is therefore realistic only within a narrow clade, in practice around the genus level; genus- and class-spanning broad-spectrum SIGS cannot rely on perfect siRNA identity and would require mismatch-tolerant design or pathogen-specific constructs. The conserved windows mapped here identify where clade-level broad-spectrum constructs can be placed, and the gene ranking (beta-tubulins most cross-targetable, CYP51C most pathogen-specific) provides a genome-guided basis for choosing antifungal dsRNA targets.

research.abstract: Abstract Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus), once a minor by-catch in the East China Sea, has bloomed into a dominant species, altering marine ecosystems. This study explored the genomic basis of its mysterious recent success via chromosome-level genome assembly, comparative and population genomics. The genome assemblies of H. nehereus and its closely related outgroup species Saurida undosquamis were of good quality, showing a 96.7–96.8% Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologues completeness. Population resequencing supports a single panmictic population throughout the coast of China. Expanded gene families and genes under intensified and positive selection are related to osmoregulation, hypoxia tolerance, immune function and reproduction. Recent selective sweeps are mostly related to immune response. These molecular signatures are consistent with long-term adaptations to a hypoxic, polluted and fluctuating environment. These findings suggest that species genomically preadapted to environments affected by global change can suddenly become new native invaders.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Effective type 2 diabetes (T2D) education improves patient outcomes, but clinician time constraints limit what can be covered during encounters. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable way to answer patient questions, yet their accuracy and reliability in T2D education across health literacy levels remain poorly characterized. Methods We developed DiaBench, a standardized benchmarking framework built from 96 question- and-answer pairs collected by clinicians from representative real-world patient encounters. GPT-5 transformed each pair into multiple-choice questions (MCQs) under three configurations (1-3) simulating different question formats and levels of user background. A five-member panel of certified diabetes care and education specialists (CDCESs), medical doctors (MDs), and endocrinologists validated the transformations, rating question rephrasing, answer rephrasing, and answer correctness. We then evaluated seven LLMs (GPT-5 1 , Gemini-2.5-Flash 2 , Cohere Command 3 , Llama-4 4 , DeepSeek-R1 5 , Perplexity Sonar 6 , Mistral-Large-2.0 7 ) for accuracy and self-consistency across three runs. Results (i) Expert validation showed a consensus over MCQ transformation. For configuration 1, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of rephrased answers were appropriate, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of MCQ answers were correct, and 95.0% (SD 0.05) of rephrased questions were appropriate; corresponding values for configuration 2 were 96.3% (SD 0.05), 97.5% (SD 0.02), and 89.8% (SD 0.14). (ii) across benchmarking for configurations 1 and 2, most models achieved high accuracy (≥95%), but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models (≥95%). All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3. Conclusions DiaBench quantitatively differentiates LLM capability in T2D patient education, with Gemini, GPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 performing strongly and other models suboptimally. DiaBench provides a transferable platform for evaluating existing and newly developed LLMs, addressing the need for standardized benchmarking before clinical deployment of LLM-based systems in patient education.

research.abstract: Summary Although wood extractives may play important roles in defense against pathogens, few studies have explored the genetic determinism of their accumulation. In this work, we have used a non-targeted metabolomic approach to perform a genetic analysis of grapevine ( Vitis vinifera ) wood extractive composition in a progeny from a cross between Riesling and Gewurztraminer. Metabolic quantitative trait loci (mQTL) analyses of cane and trunk wood extractives revealed a number of mQTLs. Analysis of one of these mQTL has led to the identification of a cluster of six UDP glycosyltransferase (UGT) genes linked to the accumulation of resveratrol-glucoside (piceid) in both canes and trunks. Detailed biochemical and structural characterization of these six UGTs highlighted a surprising functional diversity among this small gene family, as well as one UGT gene as a key determinant of the constitutive accumulation of piceid in lignified grapevine tissues. Molecular evolution analyses showed that the UGTs in this gene cluster were globally under strong purifying selection, suggesting important biological roles of the corresponding proteins. Moreover, the functional characterization showed that distinct UGT genes were involved in the biosynthesis of cis- and trans -isomers of piceid, suggesting that these isomers may play different biological roles in grapevine.

research.abstract: Supernumerary B-Chromosomes are extra genetic elements that frequently deviate from Mendelian inheritance to ensure their own survival. Their evolutionary origins and biological impacts within natural plant populations remain largely unexplored. Switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) is a model for studies of local adaptation, but reliance on a single reference genome has limited the detection of lineage-specific genomic content. We generated chromosome-level genome assemblies from the diverged Atlantic switchgrass subpopulation and discovered a previously undetected genomic element: a ~34 Mb supernumerary B-Chromosome, validated by Hi-C contact mapping and long-read depth, which indicates two to four B copies per nucleus. The B-Chromosome has a bipartite architecture including a gene-rich, single-copy proximal region (~8 Mb) and a repeat-rich, gene-poor distal region (~27 Mb) dominated by LTR/Ty3 (Gypsy) elements and punctuated by Mutator TIR peaks. High-resolution mapping reveals a highly rearranged chimera of fragments from multiple autosomes, biased toward the N-subgenome. Intact LTR retrotransposons on the B-Chromosome are younger than those on the A-Chromosomes, especially in its distal region, consistent with a B-Chromosome that arose and expanded within the Atlantic lineage. Population screening and phylogenetic analysis indicate that the B-Chromosome is largely restricted to the Atlantic subpopulation and likely has a single origin. In a typical family, 70% of open-pollinated progeny of B-positive maternal plants were B-positive, with substantial variation among families. Finally, B-Chromosome presence is associated with expression differences in A-Chromosome genes that differ between genetic backgrounds. Together, our results show how accessory chromosomes contribute to the evolutionary and genomic diversity of natural plant populations.

research.abstract: Abstract Introduction Spondylodiscitis is an infectious condition involving the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral bodies. Although Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium tuberculosis are the most common pathogens, cases caused by Gram-negative bacilli are relatively rare. Enterobacter hormaechei is an exceptionally uncommon etiologic agent in this context. Case presentation A 69-year-old Turkish male with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of prostate adenocarcinoma in remission, with no active immunosuppression, presented with lower back pain and elevated inflammatory markers. Initially suspected to have metastatic spinal involvement, spinal MRI revealed spondylodiscitis at the T12–L1 level. Microbiological evaluation of the needle biopsy specimen yielded Enterobacter hormaechei . Species-level identification was established by culture and MALDI-TOF MS, with off-label syndromic PCR testing (BIOFIRE ® Joint Infection Panel) providing supportive concordant results. The patient was successfully managed with surgical intervention and appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Discussion Spondylodiscitis due to Enterobacter hormaechei remains exceedingly rare. This case highlights the importance of considering atypical Gram-negative organisms in spinal infections and underscores the value of advanced microbiological methods for accurate species-level identification.

research.abstract: Two otherwise healthy patients from Colombia, now aged 30 and 38 years, developed pulmonary tuberculosis due to inherited, complete TNF deficiency at the ages of 19 and 18 years. We report here a previously healthy Iranian patient with inherited complete TNF deficiency who was diagnosed with both pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB between 10 and 15 years of age. The homozygous TNF variant (c.673C>T) introduces a premature stop codon (TNF p.Q225*) resulting in losses of expression and function. Despite normal myeloid and lymphoid subset development, the patient's primary leukocytes do not secrete detectable amounts of TNF. As in the TNF-deficient Colombian patients, the respiratory burst of GM-CSF-derived macrophages is impaired. Our findings expand the spectrum of TB phenotypes in patients with TNF deficiency and confirm that TNF is essential for immunity to M. tuberculosis in humans but apparently redundant against many other pathogens, including weakly virulent mycobacteria.

research.abstract: Abstract Atoposauridae comprises a group of diminutive, semiterrestrial, brevirostrine neosuchian crocodyliforms that represents a characteristic component of European Jurassic–Cretaceous tetrapod faunas. Although frequently evaluated within the context of crown-group Crocodylia origins, their highly contested phylogenetic relationships continue to obscure their precise role in crocodylomorph evolutionary history. Particular ambiguity surrounds the monophyly of the genus Theriosuchus —with some hypotheses inferring long-term persistence of the lineage in Mesozoic Europe, whereas others interpreting select Cretaceous species as representatives of separate, even non-atoposaurid clades (e.g. Sabresuchus spp). We describe a new, stratigraphically intermediate taxon from the Santonian of Hungary based on isolated cranial elements, consistently placed as the sister taxon of Sabresuchus (Theriosuchus) sympiestodon from the Maastrichtian of Romania by our comprehensive set of phylogenetic analyses using three separate datasets. Sabresuchus tribodon sp. nov. is either recovered within Atoposauridae (global datasets) or Paralligatoridae (ingroup analysis) and can be distinguished from all other representatives of these groups by a specialized morphology consisting of massive, thick-enameled bulbous posterior maxillary teeth ornamented with apicobasal ridges, an extremely short rostrum with a reduced number of maxillary and dentary teeth, and the significantly upturned dorsal margin of the posterior dentary and surangular. Comparable anatomical adaptations are present in ecomorphologically convergent extinct crocodyliforms whose inferred feeding ecology included durophagy. However, this complete suite of characters has not been previously documented in either atoposaurids or paralligatorids. Our systematic reassessment results in an up-to-date taxonomy of Cretaceous European atoposaurids and tentatively confirms the polyphyly of Theriosuchus , though more definitive conclusions require combining individual, differently focused datasets. We reinterpret Aprosuchus ghirai from the Maastrichtian of Romania as a junior synonym of Sabresuchus sympiestodon and the putative European notosuchian Ogresuchus furatus from the Maastrichtian of Spain as an indeterminate atoposaurid.

research.abstract: BackgroundElectrocardiogram (ECG) foundation models are proposed for clinical use and promoted as fair, yet such claims are rarely tested with subgroup-stratified evaluation. We measured demographic disparities across four ECG foundation models, tested whether mitigation removes them, and asked whether the dominant disparity originates in the models or in the data and the clinical task. MethodsWe probed frozen embeddings of four architecturally distinct ECG foundation models (ECGFounder, xECG, ECG-FM, DeepECG-SSL) in thirteen cohorts on four continents (5.4 million analysed ECGs, 31 endpoints, six held-out cohorts), stratified by age, sex and race. We examined embedding geometry, tested post-hoc correction, larger labelled training sets, comorbidity exclusion and low-rank fine-tuning, and compared each network with an untrained copy of itself and with logistic regression on classical ECG measurements. FindingsDisparities concentrated on age, not sex or race (median worst-group AUROC gap 0.028 vs 0.004 and 0.016; age exceeded sex in 97% of results) and replicated externally (ED-BWH 30-day MACE AUROC 0.81-0.90 under 40 years, 0.64-0.71 at [≥]75). Age formed a smooth gradient in the embeddings, whereas sex, though most decodable, carried no gap. No remedy closed it (low-rank adaptation: -0.007 to -0.004). Untrained copies (r=0.81, 102 pairs) and classical measurements ({rho}=0.90) reproduced the endpoint-specific gaps, and pretraining raised AUROC (+0.067) without changing them. The largest race effect, higher potassium error in Black patients, vanished at matched true potassium. InterpretationECG foundation models carry an age-structured disparity that replicates externally and survives mitigation. Because untrained networks and a classical model reproduce it, the results indicate that it is inherited from the age structure of the ECG and its labels rather than created by the models, so switching or adapting models will not remove it. Age-stratified reporting, untrained and classical baselines, and age-specific thresholds and recalibration are therefore needed. FundingAustrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG; CARDISENSE project, grant FO999922422). Open-weight ECG foundation models have proliferated and are increasingly proposed for clinical use, and benchmarks compare them on aggregate accuracy without stratifying by subgroup. The fairness literature documents demographic performance gaps in task-specific ECG classifiers, most often for sex or race on single tasks in single cohorts, and the remedies it proposes act on the model (reweighting, adversarial debiasing, group-robust training, fine-tuning). The one subgroup analysis of ECG foundation models we found covered two models of one family on their own endpoints, stratified by age and sex only. To our knowledge, no study has evaluated several architecturally distinct ECG foundation models along age, sex and race across endpoint families and continents, and none has tested whether a disparity found in a foundation model is also present without any pretraining or without deep learning. Added value of this studyEvaluating four architecturally distinct ECG foundation models across thirteen cohorts on four continents, including six held-out external cohorts, we show that strong average and external discrimination coexists with a disparity that concentrates on age, not sex or race, and that replicates externally. The pattern has a consistent substrate: age is encoded as a smooth gradient in the embeddings, while sex and race, both decodable, carry no comparable gap. The gap is shared across every architecture and pretraining objective, and neither post-hoc correction, larger labelled training sets, exclusion of comorbid ECGs nor low-rank fine-tuning closes it. Two controls explain why: untrained copies of the same networks and a logistic regression on classical ECG measurements reproduce the endpoint-specific age gaps, which indicates that the gap is inherited from the data and the clinical task rather than learned in pretraining. Implications of all the available evidenceFairness evaluation of ECG foundation models should prioritise age and report age-stratified performance as a primary result, because a threshold fixed on the pooled population operates at a worse point for older patients than the headline metric implies. Because the gap persists across architectures, vendors, fine-tuning and even untrained networks, switching models will not resolve it. Evaluations should include an untrained and a classical baseline before attributing a gap to a model, and services deploying these models should use age-specific thresholds and recalibration, or at minimum report and monitor performance by age band.

research.abstract: Background Cardiac arrhythmias may remain unrecognized in adults with chronic disease. Established risk scores primarily address atrial fibrillation. Objective To develop and internally evaluate an electronic health record (EHR)–based machine-learning model to identify patients more likely to receive a documented cardiac arrhythmia diagnosis. Methods We retrospectively evaluated EHR data (2018–2025) from one healthcare organization among adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic kidney disease, or coronary artery disease. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared. XGBoost was selected using internal validation, reduced to 30 features using Shapley additive explanations, and evaluated in a holdout set with data ending one day before the index date. Sensitivity analyses excluded information recorded within 30, 90, or 180 days before the index date. An atrial fibrillation/flutter-specific analysis compared XGBoost with CHARGE-AF and HARMS 2 -AF. Results Among 30,356 patients, 6,835 (22.5%) had a qualifying arrhythmia diagnosis. In 3,051 holdout patients, XGBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.894 (95% CI 0.879–0.908) and an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.792 (95% CI 0.763–0.822). At a 0.5 threshold, sensitivity was 0.564, specificity 0.971, and precision 0.857. AUROC remained 0.896–0.897 across earlier cutoffs. In the common score-calculable atrial fibrillation/flutter subset ( n = 2,436), AUROCs were 0.883 for XGBoost, 0.712 for CHARGE-AF, and 0.554 for HARMS 2 -AF. Conclusions XGBoost demonstrated strong internal discrimination for documented arrhythmias. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed to assess generalizability and clinical utility.

research.abstract: Background: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is associated with poor outcomes. Risk factors for progressive CRS are not understood in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Objectives: This study aimed to determine the incidence of progressive CRS and risk factors in individuals with CKD. Methods: Adults with CKD in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study excluding those with heart failure (HF) at baseline were included (n = 3,557). We defined progressive CRS as developing HF and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) within 12 months. ESKD was defined as needing renal replacement therapy or renal transplant. The associations of baseline risk factors with progressive CRS were examined using Cox proportional hazards models. A sensitivity analysis assessed risk factors in those who developed HF before ESKD and vice versa. Results: 161 patients (4.5%) developed progressive CRS. Traditional risk factors [multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HR) (95% CI)] associated with progressive CRS in multivariable models included lower education [1.90 (1.28,2.83)], cardiovascular disease [1.53 (1.07,2.18)], lower estimated glomerular filtration rate [0.64 (0.51,0.82)] and higher albumin to creatinine ratio [2.44 (1.98,3.02)]. Novel risk factors associated included higher levels of alkaline phosphatase, brain natriuretic peptide (BNP), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-?), growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15), hemoglobin A1C, and lower hemoglobin. Risk factors associated with both ESKD before HF and HF before ESKD were kidney dysfunction, albuminuria, and mineral bone disorder (higher alkaline phosphatase and PTH), inflammation (TNF-?), fibrotic factor (GDF-15), and anemia. Diabetes, CVD, systolic blood pressure, waist circumference, HbA1c, and BNP were more strongly associated when HF preceded ESKD. Conclusions: Both traditional risk factors and novel risk factors associated with inflammation, mineral bone disorder, anemia, diabetes control, albuminuria, worse kidney function, and fibrotic factors are associated with progressive CRS in individuals with CKD. Many of these risk factors are modifiable representing potential areas for intervention.

research.abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global infectious disease, and novel host-derived biomarkers are needed to improve diagnosis. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers due to their stability and immune regulatory functions; however, clinically validated TB-associated miRNAs remain limited. This study aimed to identify circulating miRNAs associated with active pulmonary TB. Methods This study included 90 participants: active pulmonary TB (n=30), cured TB (n=30), and healthy controls (n=30). Candidate miRNAs were screened by pooled plasma miRNA profiling and further examined using three publicly available miRNA datasets. Circulating miR-26b-5p was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations with active TB status were assessed using logistic regression, and discriminatory performance was evaluated by ROC analysis. Putative miR-26b-5p target genes and enriched pathways were explored using bioinformatic analyses. Results Microarray screening identified 108 candidate miRNAs, and cross-dataset analysis identified miR-26b-5p as the only overlapping candidate with consistent downregulation. Circulating miR-26b-5p was lower in active TB and higher in the clinically cured group. It remained associated with active-TB status after adjustment for BMI and PLR. miR-26b-5p showed an AUC of 0.867, while the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.956. Bioinformatic analysis identified 74 putative genes, with EP300, GSK3B, and PTEN as network hubs and PI3K-Akt among the enriched pathways. Conclusion Circulating miR-26b-5p was associated with active pulmonary TB and showed preliminary discriminatory value, supporting its further evaluation as a candidate host-response marker.

Interface substitutions abolish entry, whereas natural variation explains differential human EPCR use and predicts receptor compatibility across 26 animal species. These findings establish EPCR as a receptor for the Langya clade and provide a structural framework for understanding cross-species transmission and human infection potential.

research.abstract: Abstract Sugar beet (Beta vulgaris ssp. vulgaris) is a major global source of sucrose. Domestication and a history of breeding have shaped the distribution of deleterious mutations across the genome. Accurately resolving these variants offers a compelling avenue to accelerate crop improvement through breeding or genetic engineering. We combine three evolutionary methods to identify putatively deleterious derived mutations: angiosperm-wide DNA language deep learning model (PlantCaduceus), fine-scale evolutionary rates from Amaranthaceae plant family sequence alignments using PAML and PhyloP. We defined a high-confidence set of ∼5k deleterious variants enriched for alleles under negative selection. We then evaluate these deleterious mutations across a multi-study panel of more than 1,900 whole-genome sequenced wild and cultivated beet accessions. We found that domesticated beet accessions exhibit higher deleterious load relative to wild maritima, yet sugar beet carries significantly fewer deleterious variants than other cultivated beet crops. Historical trends show a decline in genetic load across more than a century of sugar beet entries in the US NPGS, likely reflecting sustained purging during modern breeding. This combinatorial method of leveraging evolutionary conservation reveals how deleterious mutations have shaped sugar beet breeding history and provides potential targets for future selection, causal-variant discovery, and precision genome engineering.

research.abstract: Abstract Biological interactions involving host-associated fungi are driven by chemistry shaped over evolutionary time. For antagonistic fungi, specialization often involves acquiring genes for novel secretions—including proteins and specialized metabolites—that mediate nutrient acquisition and host defense interactions. Here, we conducted a phylogenomic investigation of Sympodiorosea, ascomycetes commonly found in basal fungus-growing ant gardens. While Sympodiorosea and related genera (Escovopsis, Luteomyces, Manidigitorum, Escovopsioides) are canonically viewed as virulent mycoparasites, non-virulent species may also emerge within these attine-associated fungi. We explored genomic variation in Sympodiorosea to assess potential alternative lifestyles, focusing on the diversity and evolution of metabolic genes. Our study revealed a constrained selective landscape across the Sympodiorosea genome. However, outcomes of in vitro host interactions were diverse and predictable based on the antagonist's ant-species-of-origin, suggesting functional diversification. Phylogenomics indicated that gene gain/loss events in carbohydrate-active enzymes and specialized metabolism drive this diversification. Although selection acts intensely on metabolism-related genes overall, specific metabolic genes experience diversifying selection, indicating their critical role in host associations. Furthermore, Sympodiorosea exhibits protease gene expansions and contractions discordant with a strictly mycoparasitic lifestyle, suggesting either an alternative lifestyle within ant gardens or recent evolution from other niches. These results provide novel insights into fungal genome evolution and the chemistry of the fungus-growing ant symbiosis.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Individual phenotypes often depend on the genotypes of other individuals within a group. These phenomena are termed ‘indirect genetic effects’ (IGEs) and have been distinguished from direct genetic effects (DGEs) using quantitative genetic models. Recent studies have utilized high-resolution polymorphism data to enable genomic prediction (GP) and genome-wide association study (GWAS) of IGEs. To accelerate this practice, here we integrate polygenic and oligogenic IGEs using a multi-kernel mixed model. This model incorporates two random effects with a single covariance parameter for polygenic effects, while including neighbor allelic similarity to test SNP-marker effects for oligogenic effects. Our simulations demonstrated that the present model could infer a trade-off between DGEs and IGEs with a slight improvement in GWAS/GP performance. By applying our method to three species of woody plants, we found evidence for intergenotypic competition in aspen and apple trees, but limited evidence in climbing grapevines. Based on GWAS, we also detected significant variants associated with competitive IGEs on the apple trunk growth. Our study offers an alternative implementation for GWAS/GP of IGEs and thereby provides an effective tool to dissect the genetic architecture of mixing ability within a plant species.

research.abstract: Efficient evaluation of sequence data likelihoods and their high-dimensional gradients on phylogenetic trees improves inference under both maximum-likelihood and Bayesian frameworks. Here, we present BEAGLE 4.1, a high-performance library for statistical phylogenetics that incorporates new algorithms to evaluate these gradients on phylogenetic trees. We also provide new hardware implementations for both likelihoods and gradients supporting ARM NEON intrinsics and optimized matrix multiplication units -- called tensor cores -- on NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs). We benchmark the performance scaling of the library across a number of patterns and taxa on multi-core CPUs and GPUs, and compare the speedup afforded by NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as well as performance scaling with an increasing number of GPUs. We show that multi-core CPU implementations provide up to a fourfold speedup over single-threaded CPU implementations and up to an tenfold speedup for nucleotide and codon models, respectively, with performance generally improving as the number of taxa and site patterns increases. GPUs outperform multi-threaded CPU implementations for a realistic number of patterns, even for nucleotide models with a small state-space size of 4, while for codon models they provide substantially higher performance gains even for a single pattern or four taxa. Tensor cores on GPUs provide up to 2-fold speedup relative to standard CUDA cores for codon models. Using NEON instructions on ARM CPUs affords up to a $\sim 1.3$-fold speedup over non-SIMD implementation with the speedup going down to 1.1-fold at 8 CPU threads. We provide these new algorithms to evaluate the gradient and efficient hardware implementations for both likelihood and gradient calculations through BEAGLE 4.1, such that they can be readily integrated into phylogenetic software packages.

research.abstract: Abstract Rapid detection of drug resistance in fungi is becoming increasingly urgent. While multiple loci and mutations were linked to antifungal resistance in Candida albicans , the utility of whole genome sequencing in predicting resistance has not been tested thoroughly. We address this by integrating more than 1000 C. albicans genomes, with associated resistance phenotypes to six antifungals, a curated repository of resistance-causing mutations and variant effect predictors. We used Genome Wide Association Studies and Machine Learning approaches to associate genetic variants to resistance phenotypes. We found that well curated databases like FungAMR are able to accurately identify markers predictive antifungal resistance. Curated mutations were detected in 56–74% of isolates with reduced azole susceptibility and 57–90% of those with reduced echinocandin susceptibility, revealing incomplete coverage of resistance across both drug classes. Complementary variant- and gene-level association analyses recovered established resistance determinants and uncovered additional candidate loci, whereas copy-number changes provided limited independent explanatory power. Genomic prediction declined when genetic backgrounds were absent from training, and when leading predictive features differed among backgrounds. We also found that models trained on a curated list of mutations and variant effect predictors performed well when classifying drug-susceptible strains, but the drug-resistance trait was predicted with a lower accuracy. These findings support the potential of genome-based resistance prediction while highlighting the need for broader population sampling, functional validation of candidate variants and expanded resistance catalogues to improve prediction across genetic backgrounds.

research.abstract: In 2023, an estimated 13% of worldwide deaths resulting from antimicrobial resistance (AMR) were due to drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). The World Health Organization (WHO) documented a dramatic, sixfold increase in the number of patients treated with 6-month all-oral (BPaLM) regimens, from 5,653 patients in 2023, to 34,000 patients by 2024, while also documenting an emergence of bedaquiline resistance in real-world cohorts and a lack of efficacy of BCG revaccination in the BCG-PRIME Phase 2b trial against sustained Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Concurrently, the M72/AS01E subunit vaccine trial completed recruitment (approximately 20,000 individuals) across five high-burden countries, 11 months ahead of scheduled completion date. The first randomized controlled trial assessing DRTB-HDT host-directed therapy for DR-TB in adults (metformin + dovramilast), conducted at five international sites, is entering the late-stage readout phase. This synthesis of data, covering the period from 2015 through 2026, across six different dimensions includes molecular mechanisms of resistance, novel antimicrobial treatment modalities, host-directed therapy, immunity associated with regulatory compliance, adjuvants to vaccines, and the clinical translation of vaccine candidates. The Molecular-to-Translational continuum is used as a framework for the synthesis, with the regulatory immune function domain (T regulatory cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and check-point axes) linking all five domains. Our central hypothesis is that drug resistance evolution of the microbe and failure of the host to maintain regulatory immunity are interdependent and create a bidirectional relationship with each other. We have identified nine major research gaps, with milestone dates from 2026 to 2030, based on unresolved controversies regarding the bedaquiline resistance catalog and the acquisition versus transmission narrative.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT West Nile virus (WNV) is a flavivirus whose cycle involves mosquitoes and avian hosts that occasionally may infect horses and humans as “dead‐end hosts.” Human infection is mostly asymptomatic, sometimes leading to febrile or neuroinvasive disease. In 2025, Italy experienced its largest epidemic with an unprecedented geographic spread (79 provinces; 52% of cases in central Italy). Here we report whole‑genome sequencing and phylogeographic analysis of 39 WNV lineage 2 samples collected in Lazio and Campania regions between July and September 2025 from humans and animal samples. All 2025 strains belonged to a Southern Italian clade that diversified around 2020, with evidence of earlier circulation in 2024. All the 2025 genomes shared a substitution that lies in envelope protein domain III (K399R), potentially influencing interactions with the viral membrane. The same mutation was previously detected in Eastern European strains, leading to the hypothesis of introductions in Italy via migratory birds from these regions. Phylogeography identified strong viral dispersal routes within Central Italy supporting a pattern of short‑range spread and local overwintering. Overall, results highlight the roles of ecological conditions and cross‑border transmission dynamics in shaping the 2025 Italian epidemic, underscoring the need for integrated genomic/ecological surveillance.

research.abstract: Abstract Understanding how habitat connectivity shapes biodiversity remains a major ecological challenge. In particular, the roles of connectivity and ecological heterogeneity in co-variation between plant species diversity and intraspecific genetic diversity are not well understood. We combined species distribution modelling, resistance-to-movement mapping, landscape connectivity analysis and population genomics to investigate diversity patterns in three wet-meadow herbs, Scorzonera humilis, Oenanthe peucedanifolia and Lychnis flos-cuculi , and their surrounding plant communities. Connectivity inferred from species distribution models was similar across species, but it did not correlate with plant community diversity. Some connectivity metrics explained genetic diversity, but only in O. peucedanifolia . Interestingly, environmental drivers of genetic differentiation were highly species-specific despite spatial co-occurrence. Furthermore, genetic diversity of two of the three species changed with the presence of some species in the community, but it was consistently unrelated to local plant community diversity. Overall, the processes shaping within-species biodiversity may differ fundamentally from those structuring metrics of habitat connectivity and plant species diversity, with important implications for conservation.

research.abstract: Abstract Pangenome variation graphs are a powerful tool for representing genetic diversity within and across populations. For comparative and evolutionary genomic analyses leveraging these graph-based structures, it is important that graph topology reflects the underlying phylogenetic and genetic similarities of the genomes embedded within the graph. However, in metagenomic settings these approaches often produce highly fragmented multi-component graphs, hindering comparisons of genomes embedded across different components. This challenge is particularly pronounced for hypervariable viral families like Anelloviridae , whose short circular genomes frustrate existing variation graph construction methods. We present PANIMaSTA (Progressive Average Nucleotide Identity and Maximum Spanning Tree-Based Assembly), a workflow to construct minimally fragmented metagenomic pangenome sequence variation graphs through progressive assembly. The order in which the genomes are incorporated into the graph is informed by a maximum spanning tree (MST) inferred from an all-to-all genome similarity matrix comprised of pairwise Anelloviridae average nucleotide identities (ANI). Applied to over 5,200 diverse Anelloviridae genomes, we construct a sequence variation graph whose graph topology reflects the global genome similarities observed across the ANI matrix. PANIMaSTA constructs minimally fragmented metagenomic pangenome sequence variation graphs that are not achievable with existing methods suitable for similarity-aware sequence-to-graph mapping and downstream genetic analyses across highly diverse genomes.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Animal species differ dramatically in their overall size, yet the mechanisms underlying these differences are poorly understood. The Hippo pathway, first discovered in Drosophila , and widely conserved in mammals, regulates the nuclear levels of YAP1, a transcriptional co-activator that enhances the expression of growth-promoting genes. While experimental manipulations of this pathway elicit dramatic effects on tissue growth and organ size, it is not known whether, and to what extent, evolutionary divergence of this pathway has contributed to size differences across animals. Here we show that although YAP1 protein sequence is highly conserved between diverse mammals such as humans, elephants and blue whales, it diverges considerably among rodent species. While the human YAP1 protein is very similar to that of the largest rodent, the capybara Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris , those of smaller rodents such as the mouse Mus musculus and the vole Microtus oregoni show considerable divergence. An increased ratio of non-synonymous versus synonymous substitutions (dN/dS) in clades of small rodents compared to the background is indicative of relaxed constraint in these lineages, suggesting relative positive selection. When expressed in the developing Drosophila wing, capybara YAP1 was more potent at promoting growth than that of the mouse or vole. Following transfection into mammalian cells, capybara YAP1 is more effective at promoting expression of a reporter gene than either mouse or vole YAP1. Thus, by combining computational and experimental approaches, we show that evolutionarily divergent coding-region changes in YAP1 have likely contributed to the evolution of smaller body size in clades of rodents.

research.abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii is an opportunistic pathogen responsible for a wide range of infections, including ventilator-associated pneumonia, bloodstream infections, and urinary tract infections. Most studies investigating A. baumannii pulmonary pathogenesis rely on acute pneumonia models that use high bacterial inocula and do not recapitulate the prolonged infections observed in some patients. Recently, our laboratory developed a murine model of chronic pulmonary infection that enabled the identification of virulence factors specifically required for long-term lung persistence. To investigate how A. baumannii adapts during chronic pulmonary infection, we performed an experimental evolution study using this model. This approach revealed an unexpected role for the archaic chaperone-usher (Csu) pili in A. baumannii pathogenesis. At early time points, Csu expression reduced bacterial burdens in both acute and chronic pneumonia models, an effect associated with enhanced host inflammatory responses. In contrast, at later stages of chronic infection, Csu promoted bacterial persistence, potentially by facilitating adhesion to pulmonary epithelial cells. These opposing effects were conserved across two distinct A. baumannii clinical isolates. We also found that Csu contributes to bacterial colonization in a catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) model in a strain-dependent manner. Together, these findings reveal an infection-stage-dependent role for Csu in A. baumannii pathogenesis, demonstrating that a bacterial surface structure can impair early colonization while promoting long-term persistence. Author summary Understanding how bacterial pathogens establish and maintain infections requires identifying the factors that promote their survival within the host. Currently, most experimental models of Acinetobacter baumannii infections focus on acute infections, potentially overlooking bacterial factors that are required for prolonged infections. In this study, we investigated how A. baumannii , a major cause of hospital-acquired infections, adapts to the lung environment during chronic infection. Using experimental evolution, we identified a novel role for Csu pili, surface structures traditionally associated with biofilm formation. Rather than promoting bacterial fitness throughout infection, Csu pili exhibited opposing effects depending on disease progression. Their expression was detrimental to bacterial fitness during early infection, a phenotype associated with increased host inflammatory responses, but became advantageous during prolonged infection, potentially by enhancing bacterial association with respiratory epithelial cells. Importantly, these opposing effects were observed in distinct clinical isolates, suggesting that this phenomenon is not restricted to a particular bacterial strain. Our findings highlight how the contribution of individual virulence factors can change over the course of infection and underscore the importance of considering infection duration when studying bacterial pathogenesis.

research.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) assume additive SNP effects, yet genetic risk also arises from interactions between loci and environmental factors that contribute to broad-sense heritability. We developed an extended PRS (ePRS) framework for type 2 diabetes (T2D) that incorporates locus-by-locus non-additive effects beyond those captured by additive single-locus PRS or linkage disequilibrium (LD) tagging. These were modelled as interaction-informed cumulative burden (G+G; summed allele counts), epistasis-screened (GxG; allele count products), and gene-environment effects derived from cardiometabolic variables in electronic health records. Across 235,000 UK Biobank participants, five complementary ePRS models captured largely non-overlapping high-risk individuals, suggesting that a key to individual risk predictions comprises the inclusion of multiple interaction-driven biological components rather than a single signal. A composite score was predictive over traditional additive PRS and predictive of T2D among individuals whose clinical symptoms fall within normal ranges.

research.abstract: Drug-resistant tuberculosis surveillance requires diagnostic systems that can rapidly identify resistance beyond rifampicin and generate potentially actionable resistance information for routine public-health monitoring. We evaluated programmatic Xpert MTB/XDR use and characterized the molecular resistance profiles generated within a regional tuberculosis diagnostic network in northern Morocco. We retrospectively analyzed 258 Xpert MTB/XDR testing episodes performed from April 2022 to July 2026 and linked available Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra results with target-level molecular outputs. Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was detected in 203 episodes (78.7%), of which 188 (92.6%) had an interpretable rifampicin result. Molecular rifampicin resistance was detected in 75/188 episodes (39.9%) and isoniazid resistance in 71/192 (37.0%); molecular multidrug-resistant tuberculosis was identified in 51/184 (27.7%) episodes with paired results. Among 186 episodes with interpretable rifampicin and additional resistance results, 75 (40.3%) had resistance to at least one additional drug class, including 21/112 (18.8%) rifampicin-susceptible and 54/74 (73.0%) rifampicin-resistant episodes. Among 92 resistant episodes with complete profiles, 66 (71.7%) showed resistance to two or more drug classes. rpoB3- and rpoB4-associated signals predominated among rifampicin-resistant episodes, katG-associated signals among isoniazid-resistant episodes, and gyrA targets among fluoroquinolone-resistant episodes. Mixed wild-type and mutation-associated signals occurred across rpoB and gyrA. These findings support the use of routine Xpert MTB/XDR testing as a component of regional drug-resistant tuberculosis surveillance, enabling systematic characterization of multiclass resistance and molecular resistance patterns within routine diagnostic networks. Such molecular surveillance should be integrated with phenotypic susceptibility testing and genomic sequencing to resolve discordant, atypical, or clinically consequential profiles and build a more comprehensive regional resistance-monitoring system.

research.abstract: Abstract Motivation Positive selection is a key evolutionary force in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , driving the emergence of adaptive mutations that influence drug resistance, transmissibility, and virulence of tuberculosis. Phylogenetic trees capture the hierarchical evolutionary relationships among isolates, making them an ideal framework for detecting such adaptive signals. Here, we present a phylogeny-guided graph attention network approach, coupled with a novel method for converting SNP-annotated phylogenetic trees into graph structures suitable for graph neural network processing. Results Using a dataset of 1000 M. tuberculosis isolates, representing the four main lineages, and 206 single-nucleotide variants (75 resistance-associated and 131 neutral) spanning 79 drug-resistance genes, we constructed graphs where nodes represented individual isolates and edges reflected phylogenetic distances. To reduce noise and highlight local evolutionary structure, we pruned edges between isolates separated by more than seven internal nodes. Node features were encoded as binary indicators of SNP presence or absence, and the graph attention network (GAT) architecture comprised two attention layers with a residual connection, followed by global attention pooling and a multilayer perceptron classifier. The model achieved higher accuracy (0.81, AUC 0.82) than a homoplasy-count baseline (0.71) on the held-out test set. Under repeated cross-validation, however, F1 scores did not differ significantly (0.56 vs. 0.58; paired Wilcoxon p = 0.98), reflecting a specificity-sensitivity trade-off: the GAT favoured specificity (0.89), the baseline favoured sensitivity. Applying the model to 138 WHO-classified “uncertain” variants identified 28 high-confidence candidates, including rpoC Ile491Val (rifampicin, compensatory), ubiA Arg240Cys (ethambutol), and rpsA Ala412Val (pyrazinamide). These findings demonstrate the feasibility of encoding phylogenetic trees as graph neural network-compatible structures and the utility of attention-based models for detecting positive-selection signals, supporting genomic surveillance and prioritisation of candidates for experimental validation. Availability and Implementation The source code for the model can be found at https://github.com/linfeng-wang/Phylogeny-Guided_GAT .

research.abstract: Immunomodulatory Activity of Galing Leaf Extract and Fraction (Cayratia trifolia L) Against Specific Immune Response in ESAT-6 TB-Induced Diabetes Mellit us Rats The immune system protects the body against infections. However, in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM), impaired immune function increases the risk of developing active tuberculosis (TB). CD4+ T cell activation is essential for controlling Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, but immune system dysfunction in DM makes the body more susceptible to infection. Natural immunomodulators are promising therapeutic alternatives because they may have fewer side effects and can enhance immune responses. Galing (Cayratia trifolia L.) is known to contain bioactive compounds with antidiabetic, antibacterial, and immunomodulatory activities. This study aimed to investigate the potential of Galing leaf extract and fractions to enhance the CD4+-mediated specific immune response in an animal model of DM induced with the TB antigen ESAT-6. Dried plant material was macerated using 96% ethanol, followed by evaporation to obtain the ethanolic extract. Fractionation was then performed using vacuum liquid chromatography (VLC) with a gradient elution system, yielding five fractions. Immunomodulatory activity was evaluated by measuring CD4+ levels using the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The experimental animals were divided into nine groups: normal control, negative control, positive control, fractions 1-5, and extract, with a dose of 50 mg/kg body weight administered to each treatment group. The immunomodulatory assay results showed CD4+ levels of 8.399 μg/mL in fraction 1, 8.047 μg/mL in fraction 2, 6.490 μg/mL in fraction 3, 6.492 μg/mL in fraction 4, 5.917 μg/mL in fraction 5, and 7.284 μg/mL in the extract group. The findings indicated that Galing leaf extract and fractions could enhance the specific immune response by increasing CD4+ levels. Galing demonstrated immunomodulatory activity, with fractions 1 and 2 showing the greatest efficacy (p < 0.05). In conclusion, Galing leaf extract and fractions have potential as natural immunomodulatory agents to enhance CD4+ mediated immune responses in an animal model of DM induced with the TB antigen ESAT-6. Aktivasi sel T CD4+ sangat penting dalam mengendalikan infeksi Mycobacterium tuberculosis, tetapi gangguan sistem imun pada DM menyebabkan tubuh lebih rentan terhadap infeksi. Imunomodulator alami merupakan alternatif terapi yang menjanjikan karena memiliki efek samping yang lebih ringan dan dapat meningkatkan respons imun. Galing (Cayratia trifolia L.) diketahui mengandung senyawa bioaktif yang memiliki aktivitas antidiabetes, antibakteri, dan imunomodulator. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui potensi ekstrak dan fraksi daun galing dalam meningkatkan respons imun spesifik CD4+ pada model hewan DM yang diinduksi antigen TB ESAT-6. Serbuk tanaman kering dimaserasi menggunakan etanol 96% dan selanjutnya diuapkan untuk memperoleh ekstrak etanol. Selanjutnya, dilakukan fraksinasi menggunakan metode KVC dengan eluen bergradien sehingga diperoleh lima fraksi. Aktivitas imunomodulator dievaluasi dengan mengukur kadar CD4+ menggunakan metode ELISA. Hewan uji dibagi menjadi sembilan kelompok, yaitu kelompok normal, kontrol negatif, kontrol positif, fraksi 1, fraksi 2, fraksi 3, fraksi 4, fraksi 5, dan ekstrak, dengan dosis 50 mg/kg berat badan untuk masing-masing kelompok perlakuan. Hasil uji imunomodulator menunjukkan kadar CD4+ sebesar 8,399 μg/mL pada fraksi 1, 8,047 μg/mL pada fraksi 2, 6,490 μg/mL pada fraksi 3, 6,492 μg/mL pada fraksi 4, 5,917 μg/mL pada fraksi 5, dan 7,284 μg/mL pada kelompok ekstrak. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ekstrak dan fraksi daun galing dapat meningkatkan respons imun spesifik melalui peningkatan (CD4+). Galing menunjukkan aktivitas imunomodulator, dengan fraksi 1 dan 2 menunjukkan aktivitas yang paling efektif (p < 0,05). Kesimpulannya, ekstrak dan fraksi daun galing berpotensi sebagai agen imunomodulator alami untuk meningkatkan respons imun yang dimediasi CD4+ pada model hewan DM yang diinduksi dengan antigen TB ESAT-6.

research.abstract: 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across 64 species and 16 loci (L = 23,924 aligned columns; African Catarrhini and Neotropical Pitheciidae, Atelidae, Cebidae, Callitrichidae, and Aotidae) coupled with 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three independent PopSets (Alouatta spp., Sapajus/Cebus, and Callithrix/Saguinus/Leontopithecus) benchmarked against *MAFFT, *IQ-TREE/*LSD2, *PAML codeml, and *BEAST v1.10.4 The colonization of South America by African anthropoid primates during the Middle to Late Eocene and their subsequent diversification across Neotropical forest strata into five ecologically specialized families (Pitheciidae, Atelidae, Cebidae, Callitrichidae, and Aotidae) represent one of mammalogy's classic trans-oceanic adaptive radiations. Here we execute a 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across a 16-locus, 64-species primate supermatrix (L = 23,924 aligned columns with 10,254 parsimony-informative sites and 11,093 distinct site patterns) coupled with independent 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three localized Neotropical population datasets benchmarking Native Rust against *MAFFT v7.526, *IQ-TREE v2.4.0 with *LSD2 v2.4.4, *PAML v4.10.10 codeml, and *BEAST v1.10.4. Our fossil-calibrated chronogram anchors Crown Primates at 74.0 Ma, the trans-Atlantic Simiiformes split between African Catarrhini (crown 28.5 Ma) and Neotropical Platyrrhini at 43.2 Ma (stem rafting window 43.2–24.2 Ma across the Eocene Atlantic), and Crown Platyrrhini at 24.2 Ma, followed by crown radiations of Pitheciidae (19.8 Ma), Atelidae (16.8 Ma), Cebidae (19.5 Ma), Callitrichidae (14.8 Ma), and Aotidae (11.4 Ma). Codon selection modeling (*PAML codeml) reveals strong purifying constraint on Pro8-oxytocin OXT/OXTR neuroendocrine signaling (omega = 0.4905), intermediate selective constraint on TAS2R bitter-taste receptors (omega = 0.7442) and ENAM/GHR dental and phyletic-dwarfism loci (omega = 0.8436), and diversifying and balancing selection on duplicated RNASE1/CHIA folivory-insectivory digestive enzymes (omega = 1.2118) and X-linked OPN1LW spectral-tuning opsin exons (omega = 2.4891). research.abstract: Plants from distantly related lineages can produce identical neuroactive molecules, many of which have been independently adopted across human societies for their medicinal and cognition-altering effects. This phenomenon is exemplified by the traditional use of Syrian rue (Peganum harmala) and the ayahuasca vine (Banisteriopsis caapi) for medicine and ritual. Despite diverging over 100 million years ago and inhabiting different continents and climates, both plants synthesize harmala alkaloids (HAs), which inhibit human monoamine oxidase and exhibit diverse neuroactive effects. Here, we combine gene expression analyses, genomics, and enzyme characterization to elucidate HA biosynthesis for both Syrian rue and ayahuasca vine. We reveal multiple layers of biochemical and genetic convergence in these pathways, including independent duplication and neofunctionalization of an ancestral enzyme from serotonin biosynthesis, and lineage-specific repurposing of primary metabolic genes to generate a reactive precursor for alkaloid scaffold formation. Our study resolves biosynthetic routes to HAs in two medicinal plants and demonstrates convergent evolution of specialized metabolism at the levels of enzymes, pathways, and genomes.

research.abstract: Abstract Mussels belonging to the genus Mytilus are among the world’s most ecologically and economically important bivalve molluscs. Although the genus most likely originated in the Northern Hemisphere, the evolutionary history of Southern Hemisphere lineages, including the timing and number of colonisation events leading to the extant Australian populations, remains debated. Limited genomic resources have hindered the reconstruction of these evolutionary histories. In Australia, distinguishing native Mytilus planulatus from invasive Mytilus galloprovincialis is critical for biosecurity and conservation, but previous molecular approaches lacked sufficient resolution to resolve species boundaries and hybridisation patterns. Here, we present the first chromosome-scale reference genome for M. planulatus . The assembly consists of 14 chromosomes and over 51,000 annotated protein-coding genes per haplotype. Comparative analysis revealed extensive structural variation and widespread hemizygosity despite a largely conserved chromosomal organisation relative to M. galloprovincialis . Population analyses using SNPs and gene presence-absence variation in resequenced individuals confirmed previously inferred patterns of population structure and establish this reference genome as a valuable resource for future studies of genome evolution, adaptation and population genomics in Mytilus .

research.abstract: Abstract Understanding the genomic basis of stress tolerance is crucial for predicting biological responses to environmental change. Here, we investigated the genomic basis of divergence in hypoxia tolerance between two populations of eastern oyster ( Crassostrea virginica ) from Louisiana and Texas, USA. We combined low-coverage whole-genome sequencing data with previously generated transcriptomic evidence to understand the mechanisms underlying population-specific variation in hypoxia tolerance. Genome-wide analyses revealed substantial population differentiation (global F ST = 0.21), indicative of a clear genetic break between our study populations. We combined estimates of genomic differentiation (F ST ) with diversity metrics to generate a set of exploratory candidate regions showing signatures consistent with recent selection. Several candidate genes identified through this approach were associated with the maintenance of homeostasis under environmental stress. We additionally tested whether genes previously identified as differentially expressed (DE) under hypoxia exhibit elevated genomic divergence between populations. While these hypoxia DEGs did show higher than expected between-population differentiation, this pattern also holds for other environmentally responsive genes. This suggests that transcriptomically responsive genes in general may generally show elevated divergence among populations, possibly due to a weaker effect of purifying selection. Furthermore, we found that hypoxia DEGs did not show an enrichment of nonsynonymous fixed differences (p = 0.9155, as compared to the genome-wide background), suggesting that the elevated divergence seen in these genes is not driven by rapid protein-coding evolution. Together, our results support a model in which population-scale differences in hypoxia tolerance occur primarily through evolution of gene regulation acting on environmentally responsive pathways.

research.abstract: Background Diabetes mellitus (DM) increases the risk of tuberculosis (TB), but clinical characteristics associated with extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) among patients with DM and pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the clinical features and factors associated with concomitant EPTB in patients with DM and PTB. Methods This retrospective comparative study included 146 patients with DM and confirmed PTB who were admitted to Shenzhen Third People's Hospital between April 2017 and October 2022. Patients were classified into a DM-EPTB group (PTB with concomitant EPTB; n = 56) and a DM-PTB group (PTB without EPTB; n = 90). Demographic characteristics, clinical features, laboratory and immunological indices, microbiological and pathological findings, chest computed tomography findings, glycemic management, and drug-resistance profiles were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with concomitant EPTB. Results Among patients in the DM-EPTB group, 91.1% had extrapulmonary organ or site manifestations. The most frequently involved sites were the pericardium (23.4%), meninges (17.2%), and cervical lymph nodes (15.6%). Compared with patients in the DM-PTB group, those in the DM-EPTB group had lower body mass index, HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, LDL-C, lymphocyte count, monocyte count, hemoglobin level, T-lymphocyte count, and helper T-lymphocyte count, but a higher monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (all P < 0.05). They also had longer hospital stays and more frequent readmissions. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, multiple hospitalizations (odds ratio [OR] = 2.300, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.134-4.664; P = 0.021) and multiple pulmonary cavities (OR = 4.405, 95% CI: 1.349-14.382; P = 0.014) were independently associated with concomitant EPTB. Conclusion In patients with DM and PTB, concomitant EPTB was associated with poorer nutritional and immunological status, longer hospitalization, and greater disease complexity. Multiple hospitalizations and multiple pulmonary cavities were independently associated with concomitant EPTB. These findings support increased clinical vigilance and targeted assessment for EPTB in high-risk patients with DM and PTB.

research.abstract: Abstract Deep-sea hydrothermal vents and methane seeps host unique animal communities sustained by chemosynthetic symbioses, yet how biological diversification proceeds across these geochemically distinct and geographically fragmented habitats remains poorly understood. Previous studies have largely focused on either host genomic adaptation or symbiont diversity as drivers of isolation, leaving unresolved how environmental geochemistry and host–microbe associations jointly shape evolutionary trajectories in chemosynthetic ecosystems. Here, we addressed this gap by combining chromosome-level host genomics, population resequencing, and episymbiont metagenomics in the deep-sea chemosynthetic lobster Shinkaia crosnieri, a dominant species inhabiting both hydrothermal vents and methane seeps. Genomic innovations—including sensory tradeoffs (vision loss versus chemosensory expansion), metabolic compensation for pigment loss, and positive selection on respiratory protein—underpin deep-sea colonization of S. crosnieri. Populations from the Okinawa Trough vent and the South China Sea seep exhibit pronounced genetic divergence, potentially driven by Pleistocene vicariance and reinforced by divergent selection across sulfur-enriched (vent) versus sulfur-depleted, methane-dominated (seep) environments. This selection targets host genes involved in chemoreception and immunity, with coordinated signatures in both sequence evolution and structural variation. Crucially, holobiont-level adaptation is amplified by habitat-specific recruitment of episymbionts: sulfur-oxidizing Campylobacterales/Thiotrichales dominate vent-associated lobsters, while methanotrophic Methylococcales prevail at seep counterparts. These symbionts partition energy niches metabolically, with seep-associated communities enhancing biosynthesis of key cofactors (e.g. coenzyme Q, tetrahydrofolate). Host transporters for these nutrients are concurrently upregulated, demonstrating functional synergy. Our findings establish that diversification in extreme environments operates holobiont-wide, where geochemical gradients synergistically shape host genomic plasticity and symbiont metabolic specialization to drive early-stage divergence.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT China's complex river basins constitute a critical biogeographic setting for investigating genetic differentiation and lineage divergence in freshwater fishes. Opsariichthys bidens is broadly distributed among multiple, hydrologically isolated river basins, rendering it a well‐suited system for assessing mitochondrial phylogeographic structure across major river basins. Here, we used newly generated mitochondrial data to characterize broad‐scale genetic variation in O. bidens across China's major river basins. We analyzed 379 cytochrome b ( cyt b ) sequences sampled from 13 geographically distinct populations, including seven populations from the Yangtze River and one population from each of six other major rivers, complemented by complete mitochondrial genomes from one individual from each population. Mitochondrial diversity was high at the species level (haplotype diversity, H d = 0.942; nucleotide diversity, π = 0.02526), but varied markedly among populations, with some populations showing haplotype fixation and others retaining divergent haplotypes. Genetic differentiation was pronounced, with 83.84% of variation attributable to differences among populations; 93.6% of pairwise F st values exceeded 0.25. Haplotype‐network and phylogenetic analyses showed two deeply divergent mitochondrial lineages, broadly distributed in northern and southern China, respectively, with further substructure broadly associated with major river basins. Complete mitochondrial genomes exhibited high structural conservation across lineages, and the clearest lineage‐associated annotation differences were observed in the termination codons of nd1 and cox3 . Overall, these results provide a broad‐scale mitochondrial phylogeographic assessment of O. bidens and reveal a general association between river‐basin geography and mitochondrial lineage structure across China.

research.abstract: The soapberry bug Jadera haematoloma is a classic model of rapid adaptive evolution, with a well-documented host shift from native herbaceous sapinds to the introduced goldenrain tree (Koelreuteria spp.). This host shift has facilitated the insect's spread into novel anthropogenic urban habitats. Microbial associations are often critical to insect environmental adaptation. Here, we characterize the gut microbiota of J. haematoloma across native and introduced host plants, seasonal transitions, and a gradient of urbanicity. Our findings indicate that the soapberry bug gut microbiome is highly specialized, with a small number of core bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) primarily from the families Rhizobiaceae, Streptococcaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Lactobacillaceae. While traits such as sex and wing morph do not correlate with microbiome structure, the host plant acts as the primary determinant of community composition. Bugs feeding on the ancestral host plant maintain a more diverse and even microbial community featuring Enterobacteriaceae, whereas the gut environment of bugs on the introduced host is overwhelmingly dominated by a single unclassified Rhizobiaceae ASV. Furthermore, seasonal transitions drive significant turnover among accessory microbial taxa. Finally, we demonstrate that urbanization introduces a distinct ecological effect on the insect's microbiome. While the degree of local green space does not systematically alter within-host taxonomic richness, it is associated with modest change in mean community composition and significantly disrupts microbial community variance. Increased urbanization correlates with significantly higher beta dispersion, indicating that anthropogenic environments lead to more stochastic microbiomes, which may be an indicator of environmental stress. Together, these results illustrate how rapid dietary host shifts and the ecological pressures of urbanization interact to shape the microbiome of a synanthropic insect.
